answer: A gemcutter's pace blocks identity mills. A key pays 2.31 POA for one bench and a raw opal tagged with a 28-byte hologram. Over 12 hours it finishes a 14-beat sonnet cycle: seven 13-byte facets, 95 minutes apart, each signed from a fresh /23 and hashed with the hologram plus the live tip. To claim the summit bench, three cutters recompute every facet and reject a 6-byte hologram clash or two facets from one ASN. If five benches open under one wallet in 7 hours, or two holograms share three facets, all close and the 2.31 POA is slag. A late facet leaves the stone uncut; no bench is reissued.
